slot.brief: Give a compound statement involving ∧, ∨ and negation and ask which of the given options is logically equivalent to it (using De Morgan's laws or truth-table reasoning).

stem: Which proposition is logically equivalent to $\sim(p\vee q)\wedge(r\vee p)$?

verdicts.working: By De Morgan’s law, the expression is (¬p ∧ ¬q) ∧ (r ∨ p). Since ¬p makes p false, this simplifies to ¬p ∧ ¬q ∧ r.

working:
$\sim(p\vee q)\wedge(r\vee p)=(\sim p\wedge\sim q)\wedge(r\vee p)$
$=\sim p\wedge\sim q\wedge r$

Independent check: By De Morgan’s law, the expression is (¬p ∧ ¬q) ∧ (r ∨ p). Since ¬p makes p false, this simplifies to ¬p ∧ ¬q ∧ r.
solution:
By De Morgan’s law and distributivity,
$$\sim(p\vee q)\wedge(r\vee p)=(\sim p\wedge\sim q)\wedge(r\vee p)=\sim p\wedge\sim q\wedge r.$$
